artists.name: Vincent van Gogh
artists.statement: Painted fields, orchards and night skies in thick, fast strokes, most of them in his last three years, in the south of France.

artists.name: Henri Matisse
artists.statement: Made colour do the work of drawing: flat, bright fields that hold a room, a window, a body.

artists.name: Victor Hugo
artists.statement: The novelist drew in private all his life: storms, castles and dark seas in ink, coffee and soot.

artists.name: Claude Monet
artists.statement: Painted the same subject at every hour to catch the light as it changed: haystacks, cathedrals, the water lilies of his own pond.

artists.name: Katsushika Hokusai
artists.statement: Made thousands of prints and paintings over seventy years, among them the wave and the thirty-six views of Mount Fuji.

artists.name: Berthe Morisot
artists.statement: A founder of Impressionism: quick, airy paintings of women, gardens and rooms, close to the people in them.

artists.name: Mary Cassatt
artists.statement: An American in Paris, she painted and printed the everyday life of women and children with an unsentimental eye.

artists.name: Hilma af Klint
artists.statement: Painted abstraction years before it had a name: vast, coded canvases she asked to keep hidden until long after her death.

artists.name: Suzanne Valadon
artists.statement: A painters' model who became a painter: frank nudes, portraits and still lifes in strong outline and colour.
artists.portrait_source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:(Barcelona) Autoretrat al mirall - by Suzanne Valadon.jpg

artists.name: Paula Modersohn-Becker
artists.statement: Painted women, children and herself with a plainness and weight that were new; the first woman to paint herself nude.

artists.name: Artemisia Gentileschi
artists.statement: The first woman admitted to the academy in Florence; her heroines, Judith and Susanna, hold the canvas with a force few men matched.

artists.name: Élisabeth Vigée Le Brun
artists.statement: Painter to Marie Antoinette; she lived by portraits and carried her studio through the Revolution and across Europe.
artists.portrait_source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Self-portrait in a Straw Hat by Elisabeth-Louise Vigée-Lebrun.jpg

artists.name: Judith Leyster
artists.statement: A master in the Haarlem guild with her own workshop: lively musicians, drinkers and children, lit by a candle.

artists.name: Angelica Kauffman
artists.statement: A founding member of the Royal Academy in London, she painted myth and history, a field then closed to most women.

artists.name: Rosa Bonheur
artists.statement: The most famous animal painter of her century, who studied horses in the markets and slaughterhouses of Paris.
artists.portrait_source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:André Adolphe-Eugène Disdéri (French - (Rosa Bonheur) - Google Art Project.jpg

artists.name: Anna Ancher
artists.statement: Painted the fishing village of Skagen from inside its rooms: the light in a blue room, a seamstress, a maid at work.

artists.name: Harriet Backer
artists.statement: Norway's great painter of interiors: lamp-lit rooms and church pews, in a colour that is all her own.

artists.name: Gwen John
artists.statement: A Welsh painter who lived in Paris and made small, quiet pictures of women in rooms, with a very still gaze.

artists.name: Sofonisba Anguissola
artists.statement: A noblewoman from Cremona who became a court painter in Madrid; her family portraits and self-portraits seem to speak.
artists.portrait_source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sofonisba Anguissola, Selvportræt ved staffeliet, 1556, Museum Castle in Łańcut.jpg

artists.name: Eva Gonzalès
artists.statement: Manet's only formal pupil, who painted boxes at the theatre, girls and mirrors; she died at thirty-four.

artists.name: Marianne von Werefkin
artists.statement: A Russian painter in Munich whose flat colours and dark outlines helped to shape German Expressionism.

artists.name: Käthe Kollwitz
artists.statement: Her etchings and lithographs of hunger, grief and mothers are some of the strongest social art of her century.
artists.portrait_source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Denkmal für Käthe Kollwitz, Straße der Erinnerung, Berlin, 2013.jpg

artists.name: Clara Peeters
artists.statement: One of the first painters of still life: cheeses, fish and goblets in cool light, with her own face in the reflection.
artists.portrait_source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Clara Peeters - Presumed self-portrait with a vanitas still life and flowers in a glass vase.jpg

artists.name: Albrecht Dürer
artists.statement: Made the print a great art: engravings and woodcuts of a precision, and a rhinoceros, that Europe had not seen.

artists.name: Rembrandt van Rijn
artists.statement: The master of light and shadow and of the human face, in portraits, biblical scenes and, to the end, himself.
artists.portrait_source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rembrandt van Rijn - Self-Portrait - Google Art Project.jpg

artists.name: Johannes Vermeer
artists.statement: About thirty-six paintings survive: quiet rooms, a window, one or two people, and a light you can almost touch.
artists.portrait_source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cropped version of Jan Vermeer van Delft 002.jpg

artists.name: Francisco Goya
artists.statement: A court painter who turned to war, madness and dreams, in paintings and prints made at the edge of what could be shown.
artists.portrait_source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Vicente López Portaña - el pintor Francisco de Goya.jpg

artists.name: Utagawa Hiroshige
artists.statement: Made the roads, rain and snow of Japan into woodblock prints; Van Gogh copied him.

artists.name: Édouard Manet
artists.statement: The painter who shocked Paris with a picnic and a nude, and opened the way for the Impressionists.
artists.portrait_source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Édouard Manet, en buste, de face - Nadar.jpg

artists.name: Edgar Degas
artists.statement: Dancers, bathers, a café: modern Paris seen from an odd angle, with a draughtsman's line and a gift for pastel.

artists.name: Paul Cézanne
artists.statement: Built pictures from patches of colour: apples, card players and a mountain, the root of modern painting.

artists.name: Camille Pissarro
artists.statement: The elder of the Impressionists, who showed in all eight of their exhibitions: fields, rivers and rainy boulevards.

artists.name: Edvard Munch
artists.statement: Painted fear, longing and jealousy as the colours of a landscape; The Scream is only the best known.

artists.name: Wassily Kandinsky
artists.statement: Left a career in law at thirty and made some of the first pictures with no subject but colour and line.

artists.name: Ilya Repin
artists.statement: Painted Russia at work, in protest and in prayer, on large canvases crowded with faces.

artists.name: Raja Ravi Varma
artists.statement: Brought oil painting and European realism to Indian subjects: queens, gods and women, printed for the whole country.

shows.title: Orchards in Bloom
shows.text: Van Gogh in the south: the fields, the night and the faces of Arles, in paintings from his last years.

shows.title: The Open Window
shows.text: Matisse and the room: windows, interiors and the people in them, in colour that holds the wall.

shows.title: Hours of Light
shows.text: Monet at every hour: the same places painted again and again as the light moves over them.

shows.title: Ink and Storm
shows.text: Two masters of the wave and the dark sky: Victor Hugo's private drawings beside Hokusai's prints.

shows.title: Women at Home
shows.text: Two Impressionists, friends in Paris, paint the life of women from inside the rooms they lived in.

shows.title: Paintings for the Future
shows.text: Hilma af Klint's abstract paintings, made for a public she believed would come long after her. Only online.

shows.title: Seen from Within
shows.text: A concept exhibition: four women painters who looked at bodies, children and themselves without the usual flattery. Curated on Open Studio.

shows.title: A Model Paints
shows.text: Suzanne Valadon, who sat for Renoir and Toulouse-Lautrec, and painted her own way.

shows.title: Worpswede
shows.text: Paintings from the artists' village on the moor, where Paula Modersohn-Becker found her plain, heavy forms.

shows.title: Lamplight and Window
shows.text: The Dutch Golden Age indoors: a window, a candle, a table laid, and the people and things in their light.

shows.title: Courage on Canvas
shows.text: Four women who made themselves painters in the courts and studios of Europe, from the 1550s to the 1780s.

shows.title: North Light
shows.text: Three painters of the north: the quiet rooms of Skagen and Oslo, and the same long evenings turned into fear.

shows.title: People at Work
shows.text: Haulers, ploughmen, mothers: painters and printers who looked at labour and hardship and did not look away.

shows.title: Prints Across the Sea
shows.text: The woodcut, the engraving, the woodblock print and the lithograph, from Nuremberg to Edo to Berlin.

shows.title: A Room of Her Own
shows.text: A concept exhibition: women painters and the rooms, windows and mirrors they made their own. Curated on Open Studio.

shows.title: Colour Without a Subject
shows.text: Where painting leaves the world behind: Kandinsky's improvisations beside Hilma af Klint, and Werefkin's flat, dark colour. Curated on Open Studio.

shows.title: Dark Rooms
shows.text: Violence, grief and a single source of light: three painters who worked in the dark.

shows.title: Gods and Queens
shows.text: Raja Ravi Varma, who brought oil painting to Indian myth and portrait.

shows.title: Rain and Wave
shows.text: Two masters of the Japanese landscape print, a generation apart, and the weather in them.

shows.title: Modern Paris
shows.text: Cafés, theatre boxes and ballet rehearsals: the city that Manet taught his friends and his pupil to see.

shows.title: The First Impressionist Exhibition
shows.text: A real exhibition: 15 April to 15 May 1874, thirty artists who had left the official Salon showed their own work. A critic mocked Monet's Impression, Sunrise, and the name Impressionism was born.

shows.title: The Eighth Impressionist Exhibition
shows.text: A real exhibition: 15 May to 15 June 1886, the last of the group. Seurat's A Sunday Afternoon on La Grande Jatte was shown here.

shows.title: Salon des Refusés
shows.text: A real exhibition: opened 15 May 1863 (the closing date here is approximate), by order of Napoleon III, for the paintings the official Salon jury had refused. Manet's Luncheon on the Grass was the scandal of it.

shows.title: The Armory Show
shows.address: Lexington Avenue at 25th Street, New York
shows.text: A real exhibition: 17 February to 15 March 1913, the first large show of European modern art in America, with some 1,300 works. Many Americans met Van Gogh, Matisse and Cézanne here.

shows.title: Sonderbund International Art Exhibition
shows.text: A real exhibition: 25 May to 30 September 1912, in which Van Gogh, Cézanne and Munch were shown among the young painters who followed them.

shows.title: First Exhibition of the Blue Rider
shows.text: A real exhibition: 18 December 1911 to 1 January 1912, the first show of the Blue Rider group that Kandinsky founded with Franz Marc.
